hard_think: Per-query dependency hashing is not scalable; exact bytes must be sealed once and reused by a later resident authenticated owner.
A content-addressed generation is not an activation authority. The descriptor therefore hard-codes write_denial_verified=false and activation_eligible=false.
Machine-wide serialization must bind proved store identity rather than path spelling, or ordinary and extended Windows aliases can duplicate a multi-gigabyte build.
Arbitrarily long control roots are not implied by deep payload support; broad control-root hardening remains separately scored P2 debt.
dialectic_sweep: Copying the entire legacy dependency tree appears wasteful, but current exact runtime closure cannot truthfully select only imports until an authenticated interpreter/native dependency graph exists.
Reusing RECORD metadata would be faster but does not prove installed payload bytes and therefore cannot support exact closure.

Read-only attributes or chmod appear to provide immutability on Windows but do not deny the same user write/delete/ACL authority; activation remains blocked pending a distinct restricted query identity and empirical DACL proof.

The real WinError 206 falsified unit-only confidence; the smallest correction was extended-length syscall spelling at deep filesystem boundaries, not a relaxed path limit or truncated generation identity.
first_principles: An exact dependency generation binds every admitted file byte, relative path, size, and directory including empty directories.
Planning and verification are bounded by explicit file, directory, depth, path, byte, inventory, and descriptor limits.
Publication is staging-first, fully verified, atomic no-replace, canonically reverified, and fail-closed with owned quarantine.
This prerequisite completes only inert materialization; HoloIndex remains non-A-grade until exact signed activation, resident authenticated service, and independently governed retrieval RSI all pass.
